title: PSD action at the Central police station over unequal COVID-19 fine enforcement
participants_original: No direct attendance total in the opened account. A prior search-only follow-up attributed an estimate of about 20 to a PSD spokesperson; that figure is unverified and not coded. The report that 16 activists were taken to the station is not a crowd count.
threshold_50_evidence: No direct evidence of at least 50 participants. A search-only lead reports an estimate of 20, which remains unverified. Do not use 16 detained as total attendance.

title.summary: KALLXO reports a PSD action at the police station.

start_date.summary: KALLXO dates the action to 12 January 2021.

location.summary: KALLXO identifies the Central police station Qendra in Prishtina.

organizer.summary: KALLXO and CIVICUS identify PSD activists.

demands.summary: The action criticized Kosovo institutions for fining citizens for COVID-rule breaches while allegedly allowing party gatherings.

participants_original.summary: KALLXO reports 16 activists taken to the station but no total. Ballkani search lead says a PSD spokesperson gave about 20; source not opened.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No >=50 evidence. The only retrieved possible count is an unopened search-only estimate of 20.

protester_violence.summary: Police alleged aggression/contact and damage; these claims are disputed and not independently verified.

state_response.summary: Police took 16 activists to the station and notified a prosecutor. The opened account says PSD alleged police interrupted the action forcefully; beatings and crowd dispersal are not independently established.

episode_key.summary: One-day action; no continuity evidence found.

start_precision.summary: The opened KALLXO account gives a calendar date, so day precision is used.

scope.summary: One localized action at a police station in Prishtina; no wider mobilization is established.

participants_min.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical lower bound.

participants_max.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical upper bound.

eligibility.summary: Pending threshold: the opened account gives no total, while a search-only lead reports about 20; neither supports at least 50.

notes: A contemporaneous article was opened. The state-policy target is clear, but the crowd threshold is not. Police and PSD accounts conflict over aggression/force. Arrest count is not attendance.
open_questions: Can a contemporaneous body source establish total assembly size?
Can the police and PSD accounts of force be independently resolved?
Is there a reliable end-of-action account distinct from detention of 16 activists?

title: Health workers’ protest walk to the Basic Prosecutor’s Office
location: North Mitrovica, from the Health Center to the Kosovo Basic Prosecutor’s Office in Bošnjačka Mahala
organizer: Workers of the North Mitrovica Health Center and other northern health institutions; named leadership unverified in opened text
participants_original: Search-only excerpts from KoSSev, a Serbian government office report crediting Tanjug, and Deutsche Welle describe hundreds or several hundred health workers; no source body was opened.
threshold_50_evidence: Search-only excerpts describe hundreds or several hundred, but the reports have not been opened or checked for shared sourcing. Threshold remains unverified.

title.summary: Search excerpts title this a doctors/health workers protest at the Kosovo Prosecutor’s Office.

start_date.summary: Search snippets report 25 January, but no source body was opened; the date is retained as a lead only and coded start remains null.

location.summary: Reports describe a march from the North Mitrovica Health Center to the Basic Prosecutor’s Office in Mitrovica.

organizer.summary: Search excerpts identify workers from the Health Center and other health institutions in the north.

demands.summary: Protesters delivered a letter to Kosovo’s Basic Prosecutor’s Office objecting to detention/questioning of colleagues, police searches of health facilities and restrictions on their work; signs named Pristina authorities. The group reportedly worked in Serbia’s health system and its director explicitly invoked Serbian institutions as the hoped-for solution. This mixed target warrants review rather than inference from nationality.

participants_original.summary: Search-only snippets use “hundreds” or “several hundred”; source bodies and possible shared sourcing have not been checked.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The snippets would imply at least 50 if verified, but no source body was opened; threshold remains pending evidence.

state_response.summary: Snippets say a letter was delivered/received by office staff. That reception is not verified in a body source; all response fields, including accommodation, remain unknown.

episode_key.summary: One march and letter delivery are described; continuity beyond 25 January is not established.

start_precision.summary: Unknown until the reported onset is verified in an opened source.

scope.summary: Search snippets describe one local march in North Mitrovica; not verified in article bodies.

eligibility.summary: Pending evidence: snippets report a gathering, threshold and mixed state targets, but no full source body was opened and ownership is unresolved.

participants_min.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical lower bound.

participants_max.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical upper bound.

notes: Search-only excerpts report a march on 25 January and delivery of a letter to Kosovo’s Basic Prosecutor’s Office; that date is a discovery lead, not a coded physical onset. The claimed letter receipt is also unverified and accommodation remains unknown. The group reportedly worked in Serbia’s health system and its director reportedly invoked Serbian institutions as a desired solution, while the reported letter addressed Kosovo authorities. Preserve both targets and do not infer state ownership from participants’ identity.
open_questions: Can a body source establish that the reported march occurred on 25 January and verify the exact route and letter receipt?
What are the explicit Kosovo-state and Serbian-state demands, and which are directed to Kosovo state policy for MM eligibility?
Can body sources verify attendance of at least 50 and establish source independence?
Did the march end at the prosecutor’s office, and when?

title: Residents protest Kurti and Osmani’s visit in North Mitrovica
participants_original: Reports say “dozens” or “several dozen” local residents gathered and chanted “Here is Serbia” / called for the visitors to leave the north; exact count unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: “Dozens” and “several dozen” do not establish at least 50. No reliable exact count was found.

title.summary: Contemporary search excerpts describe a protest against the visit by Kurti and Osmani.

start_date.summary: Search snippets date the reported gathering to 30 January; no source body was opened, so onset remains null.

location.summary: KOHA says North Mitrovica; KoSSev identifies the Mikro settlement.

organizer.summary: No organizer identified in the reviewed excerpts.

demands.summary: Chants included “Here is Serbia” and calls for the visitors to leave the north; whether this was a policy demand against the Kosovo state or opposition to an election-campaign visit is unresolved.

participants_original.summary: Search snippets say “dozens” or “several dozen”; not body-verified and not a documented exact count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No snippet establishes at least 50; “dozens/several dozen” is insufficient, and the source bodies were not opened.

protester_violence.summary: Search snippets conflict between a police official’s statement that no incident was registered and allegations of an attempted assault; neither account was verified in a source body.

state_response.summary: Search snippets mention police presence and a statement that no incident was registered; no response is coded from these unverified excerpts.

episode_key.summary: A crowd reacting to one campaign visit is described; do not combine with the separate LVV campaign rally or later Feb campaign stops.

start_precision.summary: Unknown until the snippet-reported date is verified in an opened source.

scope.summary: Snippets describe a local crowd in North Mitrovica; not verified in body sources.

eligibility.summary: Pending evidence: occurrence and date are search-only, attendance is below/unknown at threshold, and the own-state target is unresolved.

participants_min.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical lower bound.

participants_max.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical upper bound.

notes: Search-only excerpts report a crowd on 30 January near the Mikro settlement during Kurti and Osmani’s visit; that date is a discovery lead, not a coded physical onset. The visit occurred in an election-campaign context. Chants, the state-policy target, attendance threshold and conflicting incident claims remain unverified in source bodies. Do not infer state target or protester violence from ethnicity or police presence.
open_questions: Can a source body establish whether a public gathering occurred on 30 January and verify its location?
Do attendees demand a Kosovo state policy change or oppose an election-campaign visit?
Were Kurti and Osmani campaigning, carrying out official duties, or both at the location?
Did police disperse the crowd or only secure the visit?

title: Kosovo Police Union announces possible protests over unpaid allowances
participants_original: No gathering reported; the source is an announcement that the union may choose protests if the Government does not address allowances.
threshold_50_evidence: No executed public gathering or crowd count established.

title.summary: KOHA reports a Police Union announcement of possible protests.

start_date.summary: No physical onset established; keep null.

organizer.summary: KOHA identifies the Police Union governing council.

demands.summary: Union sought payment/continuation of the emergency allowance and food allowance and a response from Kosovo Government.

participants_original.summary: Announcement only; no gathering or participants are reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No executed gathering or attendance evidence.

episode_key.summary: Announcement lead only; no protest episode established.

start_precision.summary: Unknown; no physical start date established.

eligibility.summary: Pending evidence because the source reports a possible future action, not an executed assembly.

participants_min.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical lower bound.

participants_max.summary: Unknown; no supported numerical upper bound.

notes: KOHA published a future-action warning on 21 Jan. The story says the council would choose union action if the Government did not respond; no evidence of execution in January was found. This record is a follow-up lead only and is not counted as a protest occurrence.
open_questions: Did the Police Union later hold a public protest or strike? Search for an event date, location and attendance before coding.
